name: Ventive Hospitality Ltd
title: Ventive Hospitality Ltd - 544321 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hospitality-led growth with rate-led India (ADR +13%) and Maldives occupancy gains, but Q4 EBITDA growth was 8% ex-FX gain and management gave no numeric guidance, with April–May Maldives traffic data contested.

summary.headline: Ventive FY26 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR 2,666 crore and EBITDA 28% to INR 1,299 crore, with PAT crossing INR 500 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 870 crore and EBITDA grew 28% to INR 476 crore, with margin at 55% vs 52%. Management said the reported figures include a INR 74 crore FX gain in Q4 (INR 138 crore for FY26), and underlying Q4 EBITDA growth was 8% after adjusting for FX. Growth was rate-led in India, volume and TRevPAR-led in Maldives, and annuity was steady, while March 2026 disruption from Middle East tensions and travel advisories dented the strong run-rate. Net debt fell to INR 1,484 crore (1.14x net debt/EBITDA vs 1.7x), and management said growth capex will be funded mainly from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.change: First crossing; driven by lower debt and finance cost

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,484 crore net; INR 1,999 crore gross

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 846 crore (+14%), EBITDA INR 337 crore (+24%); ADR INR 12,516 (+13%), RevPAR INR 7,952 (+10%), occupancy ~64% (down ~2 pp). Q4 revenue +5% to INR 238 crore, EBITDA -7% to INR 97 crore reported, ~6% growth to INR 102 crore after adjusting one-offs.

segments.name: Maldives hospitality
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,133 crore (+31%), EBITDA INR 398 crore (+42%), margin 35% vs 32%; occupancy 63% (+5 pp), TRevPAR ~INR 60,000. Same-store revenue +15%, EBITDA +29%. Q4 revenue +18% to INR 421 crore, EBITDA +19% to INR 198 crore, occupancy 75%, TRevPAR INR 90,818 (+18%).

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 127 crore (+2%), EBITDA INR 113 crore (+2%), margin 89%. FY26 revenue INR 505 crore (+4%), EBITDA INR 452 crore (+3%).

guidance_outlook: Management said the company does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance; medium-term aspiration is low-teen revenue growth and high-teen EBITDA growth once conditions normalise.
Visibility is limited to Q1 FY27; management expects the quarter not to be derailed, citing displaced March demand, group and MICE bookings, and a low Q1 FY26 base from Operation Sindoor.
India occupancy targeted at 75% in the medium term (Pune); Conrad and Anantara in Maldives targeted above 65% occupancy in the medium term.
Capex of around INR 1,000 crore over the next three years (Bangalore AC by Marriott, Sri Lanka Ritz-Carlton Reserve, FF&E), to be funded mainly by internal accruals.
Management said FY26 would have crossed INR 1,200 crore EBITDA without March 2026 geopolitical disruption, versus INR 992 crore in FY25 (about 20% growth).
capex_capacity: AC by Marriott conversion of Whitefield (Bangalore) is on plan, with completion by March 2027.
Varanasi Marriott is in construction and design; completion targeted in FY28.
Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Sri Lanka is in design and planning; completion in FY28, one of nine Ritz-Carlton Reserves globally.

Hilton Goa plans: rebrand and add 60-70 keys; Sol de Goa (21-key boutique resort) to be combined into the same portfolio, targeting about 200 keys together; Batim Land branded residence at design stage with capital raise planned.
Soho House Delhi expected to complete within about two years. Mundra opportunity put on hold; Narmada Estates (East Pune land parcel) identified for annuity development.
demand_pricing: India: Pune ADR for four Pune hotels averaged INR 15,152 in Q4 FY26, comparable to gateway cities; management said the company controls over 65% of the luxury market in Pune. Customer mix is about 60% foreign and 40% domestic.
Pune office absorption was about 7 million sq ft last year, with roughly 40 million sq ft estimated over the next five years; management said luxury-hotel demand is linked to office absorption.

Maldives: Q1 demand shifting toward China, Russia, Korea, Japan with shorter booking windows. Management said Maldives is connected to about 90 destinations through 40-45 direct flights. An industry data point cited by an analyst showed Male arrivals down about 25% YoY in April and about 15% in the first 10 days of May; management said it could not reconcile this data.
Maldives diesel: management said existing island stocks covered 1.5-2 months and that diesel repricing would have an impact, with timing and size uncertain.

Maldives F&B contribution to international revenue was 39% and rooms 49%; F&B grew about 39% YoY in the cited segment (management later said growth was about 10%), attributed partly to Raaya's all-inclusive allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 unfold given March 2026 disruption, and how is Pune's outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is visible only through Q1, with some volatility but no expected derailment; over time it sees low-teen revenue and high-teen EBITDA growth. Pune demand is driven by GCCs (about 20% of India's GCC market), IT, manufacturing, MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: How much has business recovered in April-May, and how much of FY27 growth is base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited displacement business from March, credit lines on group and MICE bookings, and a low Q1 FY26 base after Operation Sindoor. It said the company is moving northwards, with no quantified April or May figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and cash flow use over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of capex over three years, mostly from internal accruals. FY26 cash generation was about INR 850 crore; INR 400 crore went to debt reduction, INR 200 crore to acquisitions (Hilton Goa, Soho House), and INR 200 crore to CWIP and advances. Management said headroom to the FY25 debt level of INR 2,300 crore is about INR 900 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India Q4 EBITDA fall while revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY25 included about INR 8 crore government grant and INR 1.5 crore electricity credit income, while Q4 FY26 had INR 5 crore prior-period electricity charge and INR 2.5 crore grant. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 96 crore (FY25) and INR 102 crore (FY26), about 6% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Maldives traffic data and diesel exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged cancellations and Middle East air disruption, but cited new flights from Russia, China, Australia and Malaysia. It said diesel repricing will have an impact, with timing uncertain. Luxury resorts historically saw little dip in volatile periods.

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers in India and Maldives, and any business-leisure mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: India margin rose to 40% from 37% on ADR-led operating leverage. Maldives margin rose to 35% from 32% through occupancy, solar projects, cluster procurement and channel mix. Management saw no material change in India business or leisure mix.

risks_watch: Maldives arrivals and occupancy: conflicting YoY arrival data, Middle East air disruption, and diesel repricing on island operations.
India occupancy fell to about 64% for FY26 and 69% in Q4 (vs 71%); Aloft Whitefield rebranding shutdown and travel softness weighed on Q4.
Q4 EBITDA growth of 28% depends on FX gains of INR 74 crore; underlying growth was about 8%.
Q1 FY27 visibility is limited to one quarter given geopolitical and aviation volatility.
Execution on Varanasi (FY28), Ritz-Carlton Sri Lanka (FY28), Whitefield AC (March 2027) and Hilton Goa rebranding; Mundra on hold.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and portfolio strength, but cautious on near-term travel: management acknowledged March disruption and Maldives volatility, and gave no quantified April-May trends. It was defensive on the Maldives arrival data and the F&B/room revenue split questioned by analysts.
key_quotes: Ventive is no longer just a collection of high- quality assets. We are now operating a scaled hospitality platform with multiple growth engines, clear portfolio logic and increasing financial strength.
So all in all, we have around INR 500 crores cash today and even if I reach to INR 2,300crores debt, which was the debt as on FY25, I am sitting on INR 900 crores headroom for debt.
Maldives is connected to 90* different destinations through about 40 -45 direct flights.

growth.why: No formal guidance; medium-term aspiration of low-teen revenue and high-teen EBITDA growth, with India occupancy targeted at 75% and Maldives resorts above 65%, backed by named projects (Whitefield AC by Marriott by March 2027, Varanasi and Sri Lanka in FY28) and ~INR 1,000 crore capex over three years, though Q4 underlying EBITDA growth was only ~8% ex-FX and Q1 FY27 visibility is limited.
